changes: Resolve saved setup, clock-role descriptors and frozen V3 native clock once per track, holding the immutable source bytes and hash in a non-publicly-constructible context.
Per-event context reuse checks retained source hash, root and event/clip/cluster descriptors, plus typed containing tempo/signature identities.
Track plan retains serialized counted order and uses identity dictionaries with duplicate rejection; it does not sort or infer priority.
The existing single-event entry point creates its own context and preserves the saved-clock range contract.

first_attempt.reason: Concurrent root UI integration added nativeTrackSavedProjectClock before the Source Audio switch was exhaustive. Compilation failed; no tests ran. Root completed the switch and all source edits were held for the second run.

context_controls: Repeated shared context equals fresh saved-context projection at the bit level at zero, before and after the saved tempo jump.
A valid foreign source/context, foreign fade owner, altered retained source SHA and changed event/clip/cluster identities reject without changing subsequent valid context output.
root_composition_review: Exact child/source/current-retained cardinalities and descriptor-set checks prevent omitted, removed or unknown contributors from becoming complete track playback.
Both canonical intervals and reader-quantized windows must already be chronological and nonoverlapping.
CPRSourceTrackPlayback checks aggregate 32M input sample budget before decoding and validates each attachment/actual media hash through prepareMedia before creating PreparedProject.
Every event keeps its source rate, independently of the saved timeline rate; event gain remains applied by the direct reader after source read.
limits: Development logs are not a fixed-source final full-suite or release capture. The first run explicitly encountered an integration race.
Track tails, host callbacks, collector/normalizer admission and project mixer/routing remain separate proof obligations.
This context reuses immutable source interpretation; it does not cache across source changes, seek preparations or edited packages.
No proprietary executable was run and no Cubase output comparison occurred.
